blocks.orig: Planning a safari with Your Tanzania Trip? We partner with Chapka to offer travel insurance tailored to adventurous journeys across Africa. Whether you travel to Tanzania or Zanzibar, Chapka protects you against unexpected medical expenses, trip cancellations, lost baggage, and more.
blocks.html: Are you planning a safari with Your Tanzania Trip? Together with Chapka we offer travel insurance designed for adventurous trips throughout Africa. Whether your journey takes you to Tanzania or Zanzibar, Chapka covers you for unexpected medical costs, trip cancellations, lost baggage and more.

blocks.orig: Below you’ll find the answers to the most frequently asked questions about Chapka Travel Insurance.
blocks.html: Here you’ll find answers to the questions people ask most often about Chapka Travel Insurance.

blocks.orig: Ready to protect your safari? Get your Chapka quote here.
blocks.html: Want to insure your safari? Request your Chapka quote here.

blocks.orig: Chapka offers travel insurance tailored to international travelers. Their policies provide coverage for unexpected medical costs, trip cancellations, lost luggage, and other unforeseen travel issues so that you can enjoy your safari with greater peace of mind.
blocks.html: Chapka provides travel insurance designed for people travelling internationally. Its policies cover unforeseen medical costs, trip cancellations, lost luggage and other unexpected travel problems, so you can enjoy your safari with more peace of mind.

blocks.orig: Your Tanzania Trip recommends Chapka because of its extensive coverage for adventurous trips, including safaris, combined with 24/7 emergency assistance.
blocks.html: We at Your Tanzania Trip recommend Chapka for its broad cover for adventurous travel, safaris included, together with round-the-clock emergency assistance.

blocks.orig: The Cap Explorer policy is a great fit for safari holidays, with coverage for essential situations such as medical evacuation, trip cancellation, and lost or delayed baggage.
blocks.html: For safari holidays the Cap Explorer policy is a good match, covering key situations such as medical evacuation, trip cancellation and lost or delayed baggage.

blocks.orig: Travel insurance is not mandatory for most safari destinations in Africa. However, it’s highly recommended and may be required by certain lodges or tour operators. As medical facilities in remote safari regions are often limited, the cost of emergency medical evacuation can easily amount to tens of thousands of euros. Without the right insurance, you would be responsible for these expenses yourself.
blocks.html: For most safari destinations in Africa, travel insurance is not compulsory. Even so, it’s strongly advised and some lodges or tour operators may ask for it. Medical facilities in remote safari areas tend to be limited, so an emergency medical evacuation can quickly cost tens of thousands of euros. If you lack suitable insurance, you would have to pay these costs yourself.

blocks.orig: For that reason, we see comprehensive travel insurance as an important part of every safari holiday.
blocks.html: This is why we consider comprehensive travel insurance an essential part of any safari holiday.

blocks.orig: The Cap Explorer policy provides coverage for trips of up to 60 consecutive days. Cancellation coverage starts as soon as you take out the policy and remains valid until your departure. All other coverage, including medical expenses, assistance, baggage, and personal liability, applies from the day your trip begins until the return date stated in your travel booking.
blocks.html: Under the Cap Explorer policy, trips lasting up to 60 consecutive days are covered. Cancellation cover begins the moment you take out the policy and lasts until you depart. Every other type of cover, including medical expenses, assistance, baggage and personal liability, runs from the first day of your trip until the return date shown in your travel booking.

blocks.orig: If you travel to the airport by car, the assistance coverage also starts up to 48 hours before your departure.
blocks.html: If you drive to the airport, assistance cover also begins up to 48 hours before you depart.

blocks.orig: New to Chapka? Find out who is eligible for coverage, when to take out your policy, and everything you need to know before arranging your travel insurance.
blocks.html: Is Chapka new to you? Learn who can be covered, when you should take out your policy and everything else worth knowing before you arrange your travel insurance.

blocks.orig: For cancellation coverage to be valid, you must take out the policy directly with Chapka within 48 hours of making your first payment towards your trip. Chapka’s claims team will verify this based on the payment date shown on your invoice. We therefore recommend purchasing the insurance immediately after making your first payment.
blocks.html: Cancellation cover is only valid if you take out the policy directly with Chapka within 48 hours of your first payment for your trip. Chapka’s claims team checks this against the payment date on your invoice. We therefore advise buying the insurance straight after your first payment.

blocks.orig: Please note that cancellation coverage only applies from the date you take out the policy, not from the date you book your trip. Events that occur before you purchase the insurance are not covered. The sooner you take out the policy, the sooner you are protected against cancellation costs.
blocks.html: Bear in mind that cancellation cover applies from the day you take out the policy, not from the day you book your trip. Anything that happens before you buy the insurance is not covered. The earlier you take out the policy, the earlier you are protected against cancellation costs.

blocks.orig: If you booked your international flights before confirming your safari with us, they need to be added to your Chapka policy within 48 hours of booking to be covered for cancellation. Unfortunately, there are no exceptions to this requirement. A practical option is to arrange two separate policies: one within 48 hours of booking your flights and another within 48 hours of confirming your safari. This ensures each part of your trip is covered correctly.
blocks.html: Did you book your international flights before confirming your safari with us? Then they must be added to your Chapka policy within 48 hours of booking to be covered for cancellation. Sadly, this rule has no exceptions. One practical solution is to take out two separate policies: one within 48 hours of booking your flights and a second within 48 hours of confirming your safari. That way every part of your trip is properly covered.

blocks.orig: If you later add accommodation, a Zanzibar extension, or any other travel arrangements, you can contact Chapka by email or phone to update the insured amount.
blocks.html: Should you add accommodation, a Zanzibar extension or other travel arrangements at a later stage, you can get in touch with Chapka by phone or email to adjust the insured amount.

blocks.orig: If you’re unsure about your situation, contact Chapka directly to confirm the best option for your specific bookings.
blocks.html: Not sure what applies to you? Get in touch with Chapka directly to check which option suits your particular bookings.

blocks.orig: The Chapka Cap Explorer policy is available to residents of the European Union, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Andorra, and Monaco. Unfortunately, it’s not available to residents of French Polynesia. Eligibility is based on your country of permanent residence rather than your nationality.
blocks.html: You can take out the Chapka Cap Explorer policy if you live in the European Union, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Andorra, and Monaco. Residents of French Polynesia, however, can’t take it out. What counts is the country where you permanently live, not your nationality.

blocks.orig: If you’re unsure whether you’re eligible, contact Chapka directly before purchasing the policy.
blocks.html: Not sure whether you qualify? Get in touch with Chapka directly before you buy the policy.

blocks.orig: Yes. Zanzibar is part of Tanzania, so your stay is covered under the Chapka Cap Explorer policy. If you arrange your safari and your Zanzibar beach holiday separately, you can take out an individual policy for each booking, provided each policy is purchased within 48 hours of the corresponding payment. If you add extra travel components later, you can also contact Chapka directly to update your insured amount.
blocks.html: Yes. As Zanzibar is part of Tanzania, the Chapka Cap Explorer policy covers your stay there. If you book your safari and your Zanzibar beach holiday separately, you can take out a separate policy for each booking, as long as each one is bought within 48 hours of the matching payment. Should you add further travel components later, you can also ask Chapka directly to change your insured amount.

blocks.orig: A safari often takes you deep into Africa’s remote wilderness, far from major medical facilities. With the right travel insurance, you can travel with greater confidence, knowing you’ll have support if something unexpected happens during your trip.
blocks.html: On safari you often travel deep into Africa’s remote wilderness, a long way from major medical facilities. Suitable travel insurance lets you travel with more confidence, because you know you’ll get help if something unexpected happens on your trip.

blocks.orig: Chapka provides cover for medical and surgical expenses if you suffer a serious illness or injury during your trip. This includes:
blocks.html: If you fall seriously ill or are badly injured during your trip, Chapka covers medical and surgical expenses. This covers:

blocks.orig: Consultations with doctors and medical specialists;
blocks.html: Appointments with doctors and medical specialists;

blocks.orig: Emergency dental treatment up to 300 EUR (approximately 345 USD);
blocks.html: Urgent dental treatment up to 300 EUR (approximately 345 USD);

blocks.orig: Any other medically necessary treatment related to your condition.
blocks.html: Any further treatment that is medically necessary for your condition.

blocks.orig: If you become ill or are injured while on safari, Chapka helps cover the costs of essential medical treatment, hospital care, prescribed medication, and other eligible healthcare expenses. For trips to Africa, medical expenses are covered up to 200,000 EUR (approximately 230,000 USD per person). A 30 EUR (approximately 35 USD) excess applies to each claim.
blocks.html: Should you fall ill or get injured on safari, Chapka helps pay for necessary medical treatment, hospital care, prescribed medicines and other eligible healthcare costs. On trips to Africa, medical expenses are covered up to 200,000 EUR (approximately 230,000 USD per person). Each claim carries a 30 EUR (approximately 35 USD) excess.

blocks.orig: Yes. Hospital treatment following a serious illness or injury during your safari is covered, subject to the medical expenses limits outlined above.
blocks.html: Yes. If you need hospital treatment after a serious illness or injury on safari, it is covered, within the medical expenses limits described above.

blocks.orig: If you’re admitted to the hospital, you must contact the Chapka assistance team within 24 hours of your admission. If your hospital stay lasts longer than three consecutive days, Chapka can also arrange for a close family member or friend to travel to be with you.
blocks.html: If you’re taken into hospital, you need to call the Chapka assistance team within 24 hours of being admitted. Should you have to stay in hospital for more than three days in a row, Chapka can also arrange for a close relative or friend to travel out to you.

blocks.orig: Pre-existing medical conditions are generally not covered. However, if an existing condition suddenly leads to an unexpected and unforeseen acute complication during your trip, the resulting medical expenses and assistance may still be covered under the policy.
blocks.html: As a rule, pre-existing medical conditions are not covered. That said, if an existing condition suddenly causes an unexpected and unforeseen acute complication on your trip, the medical costs and assistance that follow may still fall under the policy.

blocks.orig: For trip cancellation, any illness or injury that was diagnosed, treated, or resulted in hospitalization between the date you booked your trip and the date you purchased your policy is excluded from coverage. If you’re unsure how a specific medical condition may affect your coverage, we recommend contacting Chapka before taking out the policy.
blocks.html: For cancellation cover, any illness or injury diagnosed, treated or requiring hospital admission between the day you booked your trip and the day you bought your policy is excluded. If you’re not sure how a particular medical condition might affect your cover, we suggest checking with Chapka before you take out the policy.

blocks.orig: Safaris are often booked months before departure, so it’s worth protecting your travel investment from the start. Cancellation coverage helps reduce the financial impact of unexpected events before you leave and provides valuable protection if your travel plans change unexpectedly.
blocks.html: Because safaris are usually booked months ahead, it’s sensible to protect what you spend on your trip right from the beginning. Cancellation cover helps limit the financial consequences of unforeseen events before departure and offers useful protection if your plans change without warning.

blocks.orig: If you have to cancel your safari for a covered reason, Chapka can reimburse your cancellation costs up to 10,000 EUR (approximately 11,500 USD) per person and 40,000 EUR (approximately 46,000 USD) per insured event. You should inform your travel provider as soon as the event preventing your departure occurs and notify Chapka within five business days afterward.
blocks.html: Should you need to cancel your safari for a covered reason, Chapka can refund your cancellation costs up to 10,000 EUR (approximately 11,500 USD) per person and 40,000 EUR (approximately 46,000 USD) per insured event. Let your travel provider know as soon as the event that stops you travelling happens, and inform Chapka within five business days of that.

blocks.orig: The amount reimbursed is based on the cancellation charges that apply on the date the covered event occurs. For this reason, it’s important to cancel your trip as soon as possible rather than delaying.
blocks.html: The refund is calculated on the cancellation charges in force on the day the covered event happens. That’s why you should cancel your trip as quickly as possible instead of waiting.

blocks.orig: The policy includes coverage for 37 different cancellation scenarios. Some of the reasons most relevant to safari travelers are:
blocks.html: Cover extends to 37 different cancellation scenarios. Among the reasons that matter most to safari travelers are:

blocks.orig: Serious illness or injury affecting you, your traveling companion, or an immediate family member;
blocks.html: Serious illness or injury to you, the person you travel with or a member of your immediate family;

blocks.orig: Death of a close family member or relative;
blocks.html: The death of a close relative or family member;

blocks.orig: Redundancy, provided the process had not started before you purchased the policy;
blocks.html: Redundancy, as long as the process had not begun before you bought the policy;

blocks.orig: Unexpected pregnancy complications or miscarriage;
blocks.html: Unforeseen pregnancy complications or a miscarriage;

blocks.orig: Tourist visa refusal, provided your application was submitted on time and you have not previously been refused;
blocks.html: Refusal of a tourist visa, as long as you applied in time and have never been refused before;

blocks.orig: Theft of essential travel documents within 48 hours before departure;
blocks.html: Essential travel documents being stolen in the 48 hours before you leave;

blocks.orig: Significant damage to your home requiring your presence;
blocks.html: Serious damage to your home that requires you to be there;

blocks.orig: Cancellation of your outbound flight by the airline when no suitable alternative is available within 24 hours;
blocks.html: The airline cancelling your outbound flight with no suitable alternative offered within 24 hours;

blocks.orig: A terrorist attack or natural disaster at your destination within 30 days before departure;
blocks.html: A terrorist attack or a natural disaster at your destination in the 30 days before you leave;

blocks.orig: A government travel ban or WHO travel restriction introduced after your booking was made;
blocks.html: A government travel ban or a WHO travel restriction brought in after you made your booking;

blocks.orig: An excess applies to each insured person. Depending on the reason for cancellation, this ranges from 50 EUR (approximately 58 USD) to 20% of the total claim amount.
blocks.html: Every insured person pays an excess. Depending on why you cancel, it ranges from 50 EUR (approximately 58 USD) to 20% of the total amount claimed.

blocks.orig: The examples above highlight the cancellation reasons that are most relevant to safari travelers. Please refer to the policy wording for the complete list of covered events, exclusions, and applicable excesses.
blocks.html: The examples listed above are the cancellation reasons that matter most to safari travelers. For the full list of covered events, exclusions and excesses, please see the policy wording.

blocks.orig: Yes, as long as the illness was not known, diagnosed, or under treatment when you purchased your policy. If you become ill after taking out the insurance and can no longer travel, Chapka can reimburse your cancellation costs, provided you submit a medical certificate from your doctor.
blocks.html: Yes, provided the illness was not known about, diagnosed or being treated when you bought your policy. If you fall ill after taking out the insurance and are no longer able to travel, Chapka can refund your cancellation costs, as long as you send in a medical certificate from your doctor.

blocks.orig: Any illness that was diagnosed, treated, or resulted in hospitalization between the date you booked your trip and the date you took out the policy is not covered.
blocks.html: Illnesses diagnosed, treated or leading to hospital admission between the day you booked your trip and the day you took out the policy are not covered.

blocks.orig: Chapka provides cover for both domestic and international flights, as long as they were included in your insurance when you purchased the policy. If your flights were booked separately and not added to your policy within 48 hours of booking, delays or cancellations relating to those flights may not be covered.
blocks.html: Chapka covers both domestic and international flights, provided they were part of your insurance when you bought the policy. If you booked your flights separately and did not add them to your policy within 48 hours of booking, delays or cancellations affecting those flights may not be covered.

blocks.orig: If your scheduled flight is delayed by more than three hours (or more than six hours for a charter flight), Chapka can reimburse reasonable additional expenses, such as meals, accommodation, and local transport, up to 152 EUR (approximately 175 USD) per person.
blocks.html: When your scheduled flight is delayed by more than three hours (or more than six hours for a charter flight), Chapka can refund reasonable extra costs such as meals, accommodation and local transport, up to 152 EUR (approximately 175 USD) per person.

blocks.orig: Should your flight be cancelled by the airline and no suitable alternative is provided, Chapka can reimburse your prepaid travel costs up to 2,000 EUR (approximately 2,300 USD) per person. If you miss your flight because of an event beyond your control, the policy can also cover the cost of a replacement ticket to the same destination.
blocks.html: If the airline cancels your flight and offers no suitable alternative, Chapka can refund your prepaid travel costs up to 2,000 EUR (approximately 2,300 USD) per person. And if an event outside your control makes you miss your flight, the policy can also pay for a replacement ticket to the same destination.

blocks.orig: Whether you head out on game drives, join guided bush walks, or enjoy other safari experiences, it’s important to know what your travel insurance covers. Here you’ll find more information about the activities included and any conditions that may apply.
blocks.html: Whether you go out on game drives, take part in guided bush walks, or try other safari experiences, it’s worth knowing what your travel insurance covers. Below you’ll find more on the activities included and any conditions attached.

blocks.orig: Most standard safari activities are covered under the Chapka Cap Explorer policy.
blocks.html: The Chapka Cap Explorer policy covers most standard safari activities.

blocks.orig: For more specialized activities, such as walking safaris, domestic bush flights, and hot air balloon safaris, we recommend checking your cover directly with Chapka before you travel, as these activities are not specifically mentioned in the standard policy wording.
blocks.html: For more specialised activities, such as walking safaris, domestic bush flights and hot air balloon safaris, we suggest confirming your cover with Chapka directly before you go, because the standard policy wording does not name these activities specifically.

blocks.orig: Most recreational sports and adventure activities are covered under the sports and leisure third-party liability section of the policy, with coverage of up to 150,000 EUR (approximately 173,000 USD) per insured event.
blocks.html: The sports and leisure third-party liability section of the policy covers most recreational sports and adventure activities, with cover of up to 150,000 EUR (approximately 173,000 USD) per insured event.

blocks.orig: Activities such as hunting, professional sports, and competitive training are not covered. If you intend to participate in specialized or higher-risk activities beyond a standard safari itinerary, we recommend reviewing the policy conditions before your trip.
blocks.html: Hunting, professional sports and competitive training are not covered. If you plan to take part in specialised or riskier activities beyond a standard safari itinerary, we advise reading the policy conditions before you travel.

blocks.orig: Take your safari with confidence, knowing your personal belongings are protected. Find out what cover is available if your luggage is delayed, lost, damaged, or stolen while you’re travelling.
blocks.html: Go on safari with confidence, knowing that your personal belongings are covered. Learn what cover applies if your luggage is delayed, lost, damaged or stolen while you’re travelling.

blocks.orig: Yes. Chapka provides coverage for loss, theft, and accidental damage to your personal belongings up to 2,000 EUR (approximately 2,300 USD) per person, per trip. This includes valuable items commonly taken on safari, such as cameras, binoculars, laptops, photography equipment, and mobile phones. A 30 EUR (approximately 35 USD) excess applies to each claim.
blocks.html: Yes. Chapka covers loss, theft and accidental damage to your personal belongings up to 2,000 EUR (approximately 2,300 USD) per person, per trip. That includes valuable items people often bring on safari, such as cameras, binoculars, laptops, photography equipment and mobile phones. Each claim carries a 30 EUR (approximately 35 USD) excess.

blocks.orig: Please note that theft from a vehicle is only covered if the vehicle was locked and properly secured, and the incident took place between 7 am and 9 pm local time.
blocks.html: Bear in mind that theft from a vehicle is covered only if the vehicle was locked and properly secured and the theft happened between 7 am and 9 pm local time.

blocks.orig: If your baggage is lost by the airline or stolen during your trip, follow these steps:
blocks.html: Should the airline lose your baggage or should it be stolen on your trip, take the following steps:

blocks.orig: Report the incident immediately to the appropriate authority: the airline or carrier if your baggage is lost, or the local police within 24 hours if it has been stolen. For theft claims, only the items listed in the official police report can be considered;
blocks.html: Report what happened straight away to the relevant authority: the airline or carrier when your baggage is lost, or the local police within 24 hours when it has been stolen. For theft claims, only items named in the official police report can be taken into account;

blocks.orig: If your luggage is delayed by more than 24 hours after arrival, Chapka will reimburse the cost of essential replacement items, such as clothing and toiletries, up to 152 EUR (approximately 175 USD) per person;
blocks.html: When your luggage arrives more than 24 hours late, Chapka refunds the cost of essential replacement items such as clothing and toiletries, up to 152 EUR (approximately 175 USD) per person;

blocks.orig: Submit your claim online via chapkadirect.com/sinistre within five business days of returning home, making sure to include all required documentation and original receipts.
blocks.html: File your claim online at chapkadirect.com/sinistre within five business days of getting home, and be sure to include all the required documents and original receipts.

blocks.orig: Yes. Cameras, photography and recording equipment, laptops, mobile phones, and other electronic devices are considered valuables under the policy. These items are covered as part of the overall baggage limit of 2,000 EUR (approximately 2,300 USD), with a maximum of 50% of that amount (1,000 EUR, approximately 1,150 USD) available for valuables.
blocks.html: Yes. The policy treats cameras, photography and recording equipment, laptops, mobile phones and other electronic devices as valuables. They fall within the overall baggage limit of 2,000 EUR (approximately 2,300 USD), of which no more than 50% (1,000 EUR, approximately 1,150 USD) can go towards valuables.

blocks.orig: Jewelry, watches, and precious stones are treated as ‘precious objects.’ They’re only covered against theft if you’re wearing them or if they have been stored in your room safe or the hotel’s safe, supported by a receipt.
blocks.html: Jewellery, watches and precious stones count as ‘precious objects.’ They’re covered against theft only while you’re wearing them or when they were kept in your room safe or the hotel’s safe, backed up by a receipt.

blocks.orig: Passports, credit cards, cash, and travel tickets are not covered under the baggage section of the policy.
blocks.html: The baggage section of the policy does not cover passports, credit cards, cash or travel tickets.

blocks.orig: Whether you travel through remote safari destinations or move between lodges and camps, unexpected situations can occur. Discover what assistance Chapka offers and how to get help quickly if you need support during your trip.
blocks.html: Whether you are visiting remote safari areas or travelling between lodges and camps, things can happen that you did not expect. Learn what assistance Chapka provides and how to get help fast if you need it on your trip.

blocks.orig: Yes. Chapka’s 24/7 emergency assistance service, provided by AXA Assistance, is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
blocks.html: Yes. Chapka’s round-the-clock emergency assistance, run by AXA Assistance, can be reached 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

blocks.orig: Whether you need urgent medical advice, emergency evacuation, or support during an unexpected situation abroad, help is always available. You can contact the assistance team at any time by calling +33 1 70 79 07 69.
blocks.html: Help is always on hand, whether you need urgent medical advice, an emergency evacuation or support in an unforeseen situation abroad. You can reach the assistance team at any time on +33 1 70 79 07 69.

blocks.orig: In the event of an emergency, contact the AXA Assistance team straight away by calling +33 1 70 79 07 69. The emergency helpline is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
blocks.html: In an emergency, call the AXA Assistance team right away on +33 1 70 79 07 69. The emergency line is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

blocks.orig: Before you call, make sure you have the following information ready:
blocks.html: Have the following details to hand before you call:

blocks.orig: Your full name and a contact telephone number;
blocks.html: Your full name and a phone number you can be reached on;

blocks.orig: A brief description of the assistance you require.
blocks.html: A short explanation of the help you need.

blocks.orig: If possible, call +33 1 70 79 07 69 before receiving medical treatment. Chapka requires you to contact the assistance team in advance so they can approve the treatment and issue a case number, which is needed for reimbursement. If you’re faced with a genuine medical emergency and cannot call beforehand, seek medical care immediately and contact Chapka as soon as you’re able.
blocks.html: Where possible, ring +33 1 70 79 07 69 before you receive medical treatment. Chapka asks you to contact the assistance team first so they can authorise the treatment and give you a case number, which you need to be reimbursed. If you’re in a real medical emergency and can’t call first, get medical help straight away and contact Chapka once you can.

blocks.orig: Make sure you keep all receipts, prescriptions, and medical documents, as these will be required when submitting your claim.
blocks.html: Hold on to every receipt, prescription and medical document, because you will need them when you file your claim.

blocks.orig: Yes. If a licensed search and rescue team is required to locate and evacuate you from a national park, remote wilderness area, or another isolated location, Chapka provides cover for these costs up to 4,600 EUR (approximately 5,300 USD) per person.
blocks.html: Yes. When a licensed search and rescue team has to find and evacuate you from a national park, remote wilderness area or other isolated place, Chapka covers these costs up to 4,600 EUR (approximately 5,300 USD) per person.

blocks.orig: This benefit can be especially valuable when traveling in remote safari regions. Be sure to keep all original receipts and supporting documentation, as they will be needed when submitting your claim.
blocks.html: This cover can prove particularly useful when you travel in remote safari areas. Keep all original receipts and supporting documents, as you will need them to file your claim.

blocks.orig: If the unexpected happens during your trip, making a claim is straightforward when you know the right steps to follow. Find out how the claims process works, which documents you’ll need and the deadlines for submitting your claim.
blocks.html: Should something unexpected happen on your trip, claiming is simple once you know which steps to take. Learn how the claims process works, what documents you’ll need and the deadlines for submitting a claim.

blocks.orig: For medical emergencies or situations requiring assistance, contact the emergency assistance team first by calling +33 1 70 79 07 69. For all other claims, including trip cancellation, baggage, flight delays and personal liability, submit your claim online via chapkadirect.com/sinistre.
blocks.html: In a medical emergency or any situation where you need assistance, call the emergency assistance team first on +33 1 70 79 07 69. All other claims, including trip cancellation, baggage, flight delays and personal liability, should be filed online at chapkadirect.com/sinistre.

blocks.orig: Provide a description of what happened and the claim you’re making;
blocks.html: Explain what happened and what you’re claiming for;

blocks.orig: Upload all required supporting documents and original receipts.
blocks.html: Upload every required supporting document and the original receipts.

blocks.orig: You can also contact the claims department by phone on +44 20 3808 7722.
blocks.html: The claims department can also be reached by phone on +44 20 3808 7722.

blocks.orig: The exact documents you need will vary depending on the type of claim, but in most cases you should provide:
blocks.html: Which documents you need depends on the kind of claim, but in most cases you should supply:

blocks.orig: Your policy number and insurance certificate;
blocks.html: Your policy number and insurance certificate;

blocks.orig: Original receipts for all expenses you’re claiming;
blocks.html: Original receipts for every expense you’re claiming;

blocks.orig: For medical claims: prescriptions, medical certificates confirming the diagnosis, the date, and nature of the illness or injury, and hospital admission records, where applicable;
blocks.html: For medical claims: prescriptions, medical certificates stating the diagnosis, the date and nature of the illness or injury, and hospital admission records, if relevant;

blocks.orig: For cancellation claims: a medical certificate issued by your doctor (if the claim is illness-related), together with proof of the cancellation charges from your travel provider;
blocks.html: For cancellation claims: a medical certificate from your doctor (when the claim relates to illness), along with proof of the cancellation charges from your travel provider;

blocks.orig: For baggage theft: a police report submitted within 24 hours of the incident;
blocks.html: For stolen baggage: a police report filed within 24 hours of the incident;

blocks.orig: For flight delays or cancellations: written confirmation from the airline or carrier explaining the reason for the disruption and the length of the delay.
blocks.html: For flight delays or cancellations: written confirmation from the airline or carrier stating why the disruption happened and how long the delay was.

blocks.orig: Report your claim as soon as possible after the incident. The required timeframe depends on the type of claim:
blocks.html: Report your claim as soon as you can after the incident. How long you have depends on the type of claim:

blocks.orig: Cancellation claims: notify Chapka within five business days after informing your travel provider of the cancellation;
blocks.html: Cancellation claims: let Chapka know within five business days of telling your travel provider about the cancellation;

blocks.orig: Baggage claims: submit your claim within five business days of returning home;
blocks.html: Baggage claims: file your claim within five business days of getting home;

blocks.orig: Medical assistance: contact the assistance team immediately, or as soon as possible if an emergency prevented you from calling beforehand.
blocks.html: Medical assistance: call the assistance team straight away, or as soon as you can if an emergency stopped you calling first.

blocks.orig: Submitting your claim within the required deadlines and providing all supporting documents will help avoid unnecessary delays in processing.
blocks.html: Filing your claim within the deadlines and supplying every supporting document helps prevent needless delays in handling it.

blocks.orig: AXA Partners aims to confirm receipt of your claim within ten working days and to provide a final response within a maximum of two months. More complex claims may require additional time to assess.
blocks.html: AXA Partners aims to acknowledge your claim within ten working days and to give a final answer within two months at most. More complicated claims may take longer to assess.

blocks.orig: Submitting all required documents at the start of the process can help speed up your claim. Missing information or incomplete documentation is one of the most common reasons for delays.
blocks.html: Sending all the required documents at the beginning can speed up your claim. Missing details or incomplete paperwork are among the most frequent causes of delay.

blocks.orig: Find out who to contact if you need help before, during or after your trip.
blocks.html: See who to get in touch with if you need help before, during or after your trip.

blocks.orig: For medical emergencies and urgent assistance during your trip, always contact Chapka directly at +33 1 70 79 07 69. They have the medical expertise and resources to provide immediate assistance. For questions about the policy, coverage, eligibility, claims or whether the insurance is suitable for your situation, Chapka is also your first point of contact.
blocks.html: In a medical emergency or when you need urgent help on your trip, always call Chapka directly on +33 1 70 79 07 69. They have the medical know-how and resources to help you straight away. Chapka is also the first place to go with questions about the policy, cover, eligibility, claims or whether the insurance suits your situation.

blocks.orig: This page provides a summary of the main features of the Chapka Cap Explorer policy. For complete details, please refer to the official policy documents below.
